title: Vendor Layout Spillover: Does Adjacency Confound the Market-Day Effect on Sales?
one_line: Use instrumental-variable-like reasoning on sparse, non-random vendor placement to separate the causal effect of foot traffic (day-of-week) from locational advantage, where standard causal adjustment fails because treatment is spatially embedded.
self_assessment: Has legs: the tension between observational causal inference (built for independent units) and spatial-network data (where treatment and confounders are entangled by geography) forces a genuine methodological compromise that exposes the limits of covariate adjustment.

title: Temporal Hypergraph Collapse: Detecting Brood-Pattern Asymmetries via Time-Windowed Subgraph Isomorphism
one_line: Can we detect early colony disease spread by comparing observed nurse→brood contact networks against the null model of 'symmetric diffusion,' where the technique fails unless we collapse temporal hyperedges into directed time-lagged digraphs?
self_assessment: The seam is real: standard network analysis treats contacts as undirected snapshots, but brood disease propagation is causal (nurse→brood, not vice versa) and time-indexed; we must engineer directed lagged edges from temporal contact sequences. This forces explicit handling of the temporal asymmetry rather than applying off-the-shelf centrality.
